P1: In Jan 2026 Roblox added an Async suffix to 46 yielding methods. Use Player:LoadCharacterAsync, BadgeService:AwardBadgeAsync and MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync. Instance:WaitForChild and RemoteFunction:InvokeServer were NOT renamed (nor InvokeClient or BindableFunction:Invoke), so keep those names. The old names still work and behave the same. They are deprecated for information only, with no removal scheduled, but Script Analysis flags them. Write new code with the Async names. Because they yield and can fail, wrap them in pcall.
P2: Turn it on at Workspace > Server Authority by setting AuthorityMode = Server (full release July 2026). It forces these settings: NextGenerationReplication = Enabled, PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem = Enabled, SignalBehavior = Deferred, StreamingEnabled = Enabled and UseFixedSimulation = Enabled. Put predicted gameplay logic in a function registered with RunService:BindToSimulation(fn). It runs on both client and server and can re-run during resimulation (rollback), so it must be deterministic. Read input from InputAction state, not UserInputService events. Inside that logic use time() as the clock, because tick(), os.time() and os.clock() are not rolled back. Do not Destroy or reparent inside bound functions. Keep rendering, sound and VFX in RenderStepped and make them tolerate rollback. Only the first 64 attributes replicate.
P3: The property is Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem. Timeline: from June 2026 it defaults to Disabled (opt-in). Early 2027 the default becomes Enabled (planned). Mid 2027 the property and the old player scripts are removed (planned, and earlier rollouts have slipped). Server Authority mode forces it to Enabled. Code at risk: anything that calls PlayerModule internals, such as require(PlayerModule):GetControls() or Enable/Disable on controls; code that relies on the old ContextActionService input sinking or priorities; forked or copied PlayerModule/ControlModule scripts, which need StarterPlayer.CreateDefaultPlayerModule handling; and custom movement that hooks the old control modules. Also never bind the same key to the same action in both ContextActionService and the Input Action System, or it fires twice.
P4: As of the Oct 21 2026 announcement, all user-to-user chat must go through TextChatService. Scripts reading TextChatMessage.Text or .Translation get empty strings, with a warning. OnIncomingMessage and Player.Chatted are no longer supported for custom moderation or filtering, and PrefixText is unsupported (native prefixes are planned for early 2027). Custom chat UI must move to TextChannelWindow (which can sit on a SurfaceGui). Custom commands move to TextChatCommand and preset messages to Quick Words. Other user text, such as signs or pet names, must be filtered and limited to one submission per minute, or sent through a TextChannel. Timeline: opt in now with TextChatService.PlatformIntegratedChat = Enabled; automatic opt-in in Feb 2027 (opt-out possible); required in May 2027.
P5: Since 2026-07-29, limits are experience-wide budgets shared by all servers and Open Cloud, per minute. Standard write = 300 + 20 x CCU (the base was 250 before). Read = 300 + 40 x CCU, List = 300 + 2 x CCU, Remove = 300 + 40 x CCU, and ordered write = 300 + 20 x CCU. Per-server limits still apply (roughly 60 + 40 x players for read and write). Per key, the rolling 60 s limit is 25 MB read and 4 MB write, with each request rounded up to the next KB. Each request queue holds about 30 requests; overflow gives errors 301-306. Storage = 500 MB + 1 MB per lifetime user, compressed, counting latest versions only. UpdateAsync counts as one read plus one write against the budgets. Open Cloud bulk jobs draw from the same pool.
P6: Before purchase, show every possible outcome with its numerical odds as percentages that add up to 100%. A long list can sit behind a clearly labelled Info or Details button; a bare (i) icon is not enough. The rule also covers indirect purchases: Gems bought with Robux and then spent on crates count. The Luck Potion must state its effect numerically before it is bought, and the displayed odds must update while it is active. One-time outcomes must update the odds shown to that player. Generate the displayed odds and the actual roll from the same table. For each player, check on the server: PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync(player).ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted. If it is true, block paid crate purchases or offer an alternative, such as a free path, a direct sale or hiding the item. Also check IsPaidItemTradingAllowed and block trading of paid outcomes when it is false. Gate the purchase in the server remote, not just the UI.

G1: Rules: have exactly one ProcessReceipt handler for all products, assigned once. Find the player; if they are gone, or their data is not loaded, locked or unable to save, return NotProcessedYet. Check whether PurchaseId has already been granted and stored in the player's saved data; if so, return PurchaseGranted without granting again. Otherwise grant and record the PurchaseId in the same mutation and the same DataStore key, save with UpdateAsync inside pcall, and return PurchaseGranted only after the save succeeds. Return NotProcessedYet on any error. Never yield forever, and never grant in PromptProductPurchaseFinished. Charged but nothing received: the handler returned PurchaseGranted before a successful save (or crashed or errored), or the player left, or a second script overwrote ProcessReceipt. Received twice: Roblox retries receipts that are not granted, and without a PurchaseId record (or with the grant and the record in different keys) the retry grants again. Keep a bounded list of recent PurchaseIds.
G2: Use UpdateAsync whenever the new value depends on the old one, or when several servers may write the same key: player profiles, currency, purchases, session locks. It is atomic read-modify-write, so if another server wrote in between, your transform re-runs with the newer value. SetAsync blindly overwrites and can clobber newer data; GetAsync followed by SetAsync races. Transform rules: it gets (currentValue, keyInfo), where keyInfo is nil for a new key. It must not yield: no task.wait, no other Async calls, no remote invokes. It must be pure and side-effect free, because it may run several times. Return nil to cancel the write; the call still succeeds. Return newValue, userIds, metadata, passing keyInfo:GetUserIds() and GetMetadata() through, or they are cleared. Do not mutate a captured live table. Validate the stored value (session lock, version) inside the transform. UpdateAsync costs one read plus one write.
G3:
It is not safe. (1) typeof(gold) == 'number' accepts NaN, inf and fractions. NaN fails both comparisons (NaN < 0 and NaN > x are both false), so it passes. Fractions such as 0.5 and 0 also pass. (2) It reads player.Gold.Value, which is fine if that value is server-owned, but the gold is not reserved, so the player can spam offers or spend the gold elsewhere before the trade completes (a double-spend race). (3) There is no rate limit and no check of trade state or partner. Fix:
```lua
local last = {}
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
  if typeof(gold) ~= 'number' or gold ~= gold or gold % 1 ~= 0 then return end
  if gold <= 0 or gold > player.Gold.Value then return end
  local t = os.clock(); if last[player] and t - last[player] < 0.5 then return end; last[player] = t
  if not isInActiveTrade(player) then return end
  createOffer(player, gold) -- reserve/escrow gold server-side; re-validate at commit
end)
```
Validate again atomically when the trade is committed, and clear last[player] on PlayerRemoving.
G4: The Animator writes Motor6D.Transform for every joint that a playing track keys, each frame after PreAnimation. A Heartbeat write happens after physics has already used Transform and is overwritten by the next animation step, so the aim gets wiped. Write procedural offsets in RunService.PreSimulation (formerly Stepped), which runs after the Animator and before physics reads Transform. Compose with the animated value instead of replacing it: motor.Transform = aimCF * motor.Transform (outside the animation) or motor.Transform * aimCF (inside). Do not keep multiplying onto joints that no track keys, or the rotation winds up; store a base value. Edit C0 instead for static or rest offsets, such as a mount or grip position or a permanent re-pose: the Animator never writes C0, and C0 replicates from the server. On AnimationConstraint joints (Avatar Joint Upgrade) there is no C0, so use Transform.
G5: Priority is resolved per joint. A track competes only on joints it actually keys, with weight > 0. Priorities from low to high: Core, Idle, Movement, Action, Action2, Action3, Action4 (compare by order, not .Value). On each joint the highest-priority track wins. If the walk animation is Movement and the swing is also Movement (or Core, which is the default for uploaded animations), they blend or the walk dominates, so the swing looks weak. Equal priorities blend by weight: two tracks at weight 1 give a 50/50 mix. Weights are allocated from the highest priority down. When the summed weights fit in the remaining weight, each track gets its own weight, otherwise they share proportionally. If the total is below 1, the pose is pulled toward rest. Fix: set the swing's Priority to Action (or higher) in the editor or with track.Priority, play it at weight 1 (AdjustWeight), and remove leg keys from the swing so the legs still walk.
G6: FBX uses centimetres. Blender's default metre scene, exported with the default unit settings, writes a 100x unit factor, and Studio's importer reads that as centimetre-to-stud scaling, so the model comes in about 100x too big. Recommended: in Blender use Scene Units = None (or keep Unit Scale fixed so 1 unit = 1 stud), apply rotation and scale (Ctrl+A) first, then export FBX with Transform > Apply Scalings = FBX Unit Scale, Forward = -Z or Z per the docs, Up = Y, Apply Unit on, Add Leaf Bones off, Bake Animation off unless needed, and Path Mode = Copy with embedded textures. In the Studio importer, check the Scale Unit (Stud) and the World Forward and Up settings. Do not fix it by rescaling in Studio, and do not mix several scale fixes. Exporting GLB avoids the FBX unit problem.
G7: Mirror and Bevel are live modifiers, and the glTF/GLB exporter writes only the base mesh unless modifiers are applied. Without that, you get half the mesh (the Mirror is gone) and hard edges (the Bevel is gone). Fix: tick Include/Mesh > Apply Modifiers in the glTF export dialog, or apply the modifiers yourself (Ctrl+A on each, or Object > Convert > Mesh) on a copy. The catch: the exporter cannot apply modifiers to a mesh with shape keys, which are skipped or dropped. Applying them also bakes the result, so the Mirror symmetry and Bevel settings are no longer editable, and on rigged meshes you must not apply the Armature modifier. Order matters (Mirror with Clipping and Merge before Bevel). Apply rotation and scale and Merge by Distance afterwards. Keep a non-destructive source file.
G8: Problem 1: fromScale(0.3, 0.3) is 30% of the width and 30% of the height. Screens have different aspect ratios, so the frame is not square and stretches. Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (AspectRatio = 1, or the shape you want), or use SizeConstraint = RelativeYY, plus optional UISizeConstraint min/max limits. Problem 2: the button sits in the device unsafe area or under the Roblox top bar. Fix: set ScreenGui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets (the default for interactive UI; avoid None and the legacy IgnoreGuiInset for controls), set SafeAreaCompatibility explicitly, and position the button with an offset margin. If you align with the top bar, read GuiService.TopbarInset live through GetPropertyChangedSignal instead of hard-coding 36 px or using GetGuiInset. Put full-bleed backgrounds in a separate ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = None.

```lua
local RS = game:GetService('ReplicatedStorage')
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local Items = require(RS.Shared.ItemConfig) -- server-trusted prices
local last = {}
RS.Remotes.BuyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
  local t = os.clock()
  if last[player] and t - last[player] < 0.25 then return end
  last[player] = t
  if typeof(itemId) ~= 'string' or #itemId > 50 then return end
  if typeof(quantity) ~= 'number' or quantity ~= quantity or quantity % 1 ~= 0 then return end
  if quantity < 1 or quantity > 99 then return end
  local item = Items[itemId]
  if not item or not item.Purchasable then return end
  local data = PlayerData.get(player) -- server-owned profile
  if not data then return end
  local cost = item.Price * quantity
  if data.Coins < cost then return end
  data.Coins -= cost
  data.Inventory[itemId] = (data.Inventory[itemId] or 0) + quantity
end)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)
```
The price comes from the server, never from the client. Types are validated, NaN and inf are rejected, quantity is a bounded integer, requests are rate-limited, and the deduction and grant happen with no yield in between.
T2:
```lua
-- load
local function load(player)
  local token = HttpService:GenerateGUID(false)
  for attempt = 1, 5 do
    local ok, res = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(d)
      d = d or default()
      local lock = d.Lock
      if lock and lock.Token ~= token and os.time() - lock.Time < 90 then return nil end -- locked elsewhere
      d.Lock = {Token = token, JobId = game.JobId, Time = os.time()}
      return d
    end)
    if ok and res and res.Lock.Token == token then return res, token end
    task.wait(attempt * 2) -- locked or failed: retry; never hand out defaults
  end
  player:Kick('Data busy, rejoin')
end
-- save (autosave every ~60 s renews the lease; final save releases it)
local function save(player, release)
  store:UpdateAsync(key(player), function(d)
    if not d or not d.Lock or d.Lock.Token ~= session[player].token then return nil end -- fenced: lost lock
    d.Data = session[player].data
    d.Lock = (not release) and {Token = d.Lock.Token, JobId = game.JobId, Time = os.time()} or nil
    return d
  end)
end
```
Call save(p, true) on PlayerRemoving and in BindToClose. Before teleporting, do the final save and release the lock. The destination server waits for the lock to be released or expire. The lease (90 s) must be longer than the autosave interval. Trades and purchases only change locked, loaded data.

T4: FireServer automatically passes the firing player as the first argument on the server. The client also passed LocalPlayer, so on the server player = the auto player, amount = the LocalPlayer Instance and 50 is the third argument. amount + 1 is therefore arithmetic on an Instance. Fix the client: remote:FireServer(50). On the server, validate anyway: if typeof(amount) ~= 'number' or amount ~= amount then return end. Never trust a player argument sent by the client; always use the implicit first parameter.
T5:
In Studio solo play, the player can join before the server Script has run and connected PlayerAdded, so the event never fires for that first player. (Live servers start before players arrive, so it works there.) The standard fix is to handle players who are already present after connecting:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local function onPlayerAdded(player) --[[create leaderstats]] end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p) end
```
Also avoid yields (WaitForChild or DataStore calls) before the Connect line, and keep the function idempotent.

Hierarchy (for example in StarterPlayerScripts or ReplicatedStorage, cloned to the client): InputContext 'Gameplay' (Enabled = true, Priority = 1000) > InputAction 'Sprint' (Type = Bool) > three InputBindings: KeyCode = LeftShift (or LeftControl if shift-lock is on), KeyCode = ButtonL3, and UIButton = a TextButton in your HUD for touch.

local ctx = Instance.new('InputContext'); ctx.Name = 'Gameplay'; ctx.Priority = 1000
local sprint = Instance.new('InputAction'); sprint.Name = 'Sprint'; sprint.Type = Enum.InputActionType.Bool; sprint.Parent = ctx
local function bind(props) local b = Instance.new('InputBinding'); for k, v in props do b[k] = v end; b.Parent = sprint end
bind({KeyCode = Enum.KeyCode.LeftShift})
bind({KeyCode = Enum.KeyCode.ButtonL3})
bind({UIButton = Players.LocalPlayer.PlayerGui:WaitForChild('HUD'):WaitForChild('SprintButton')})
ctx.Parent = Players.LocalPlayer:WaitForChild('PlayerScripts')
local BASE = 16
local function hum() local c = Players.LocalPlayer.Character; return c and c:FindFirstChildOfClass('Humanoid') end
sprint.Pressed:Connect(function() local h = hum(); if h then h.WalkSpeed = BASE * 2 end end)
sprint.Released:Connect(function() local h = hum(); if h then h.WalkSpeed = BASE end end)

You can also use sprint.StateChanged or sprint:GetState(). Gotcha: Shift conflicts with shift-lock, so move sprint off Shift or disable EnableMouseLockOption. Do not also bind the key with ContextActionService.
T8: Your game has Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs enabled. That is the 2026 mesh streaming and cloud LoD system: opt-in from April 2026, with the default planned to become Enabled. When it is on, every mesh uses automatically generated cloud LoDs and streams, and MeshPart.RenderFidelity is ignored. That is why Precise does nothing and the meshes still drop detail at distance. Check the effective value of the Workspace property in Studio. Your options: disable it while that is still allowed (it is planned to be removed later), or work with the system by keeping detail in the silhouette, budgeting triangles at the source and testing at real distances. Don't rely on RenderFidelity for quality or performance going forward.
